title: preventive-plan.json
description: Authoritative shape for the preventive recommender's decision plan. Produced by skills/generate-preventive-recommend at .service-approval/<slug>/05-recommended-guidance/preventive-plan.json. Consumed by the preventive authoring sub-skills (generate-preventive-scp/-rcp/-iam) and the root-cause critic. The plan is the gate: each GENERATE_* decision MUST carry a non-null anchor; ROUTE_DETECTIVE / REFER_TO_REFERENCE decisions carry no anchor. additionalProperties:false at top level and inside decisions[] to catch drift; permissive inside _metadata.

source_control_id.$comment: The originating control id from mapping-results.json that this decision implements. Cross-checked at validate time against mapping-results.json so an orphan decision (no matching control upstream) hard-fails.

plan_actions.$comment: The reviewed action set: the IAM actions the recommender deliberately intends this control's authored policy to gate. The root-cause critic rejects any authored Deny action absent from this set — an action the enforcing key happens to apply to but that was never reviewed is silent scope-creep. When omitted, the critic falls back to the mapping control's actions[].

citation.$comment: Typed citation for the intent source — what motivates the control. type==canopy: cite the Canopy mitigation/implementation alias in id; when the Canopy implementation carries a public REFERENCE href, include it as url (MCP-verified, verified_via==mcp). type==reference: cite the reference-repo example in id and url. type==catalog: cite the AWS Control Catalog ARN in id. type==service-doc: cite the AWS doc URL in url.

allOf.$comment: type==canopy MUST cite the alias in id.
A canopy citation carrying a url must mark it MCP-verified.

application_guidance.$comment: Concrete 'what to do with this policy' instructions for the customer, for authored (GENERATE_*) AND referred (REFER_TO_REFERENCE) decisions. placement = where the policy goes; placeholders[] = the specific tokens the customer must edit (account ids, ORG ids, role/function ARNs, OUs), drawn from the control's real parameter/condition names; test = how to verify it works before relying on it; rollback = how to undo it. For a referred control, this summarizes how to copy the reference example and what to change — not just the URL.

applicability.$comment: What resource subset the cited policy targets and how to use it — including where NOT to apply it. Expected when the decision surfaces a citation URL (anchor.url or citation.url); omit for a canopy-only citation with no URL. applies_to = the specific resource subset/type the policy targets and the pattern that selects it, drawn from the control's real parameters/condition keys and the reference example's placeholders. usage_notes = how the customer is meant to use it, including the caution about where NOT to apply it.

allOf.$comment: Every GENERATE_* decision MUST carry a non-null anchor with an example_id — the repo-anchor gate.
ROUTE_DETECTIVE means not preventable and routed; no anchor.

When a preventive decision surfaces a citation URL to the customer, applicability MUST be present (with non-empty applies_to + usage_notes) so the report can explain what the cited policy targets and where not to apply it. Excludes ROUTE_DETECTIVE — a routed objective surfaces no preventive policy to clarify even when its citation carries a service-doc URL. The anchor.url case is enforced deterministically in validate_reference_anchor.py (cross-two-url conditionals are awkward in pure JSON Schema).
